text.p: The Italian lower house of parliament on Sunday approved the government's 1997 austerity budget, passing the bill into law.

The package is designed to cut 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's project deficit in a last minute bid to to prepare Italy for the planned launch of the single European currency in 1999.

The budget was approved by 316 votes to two, with two abstentions. The centre-right Freedom Alliance, headed by media mogul Silvio Berlusconi, and the secessionist Northern League party, boycotted the final vote in protest against the package.

Opposition parties have criticised Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government for relying too heavily on tax hikes in its efforts to make Italy a founder member of European monetary and economic union (EMU).

And despite the tough nature of the budget, a growing number of economists believe that additional financial measures will be needed early next year if Italy is to meet the exacting criteria laid down for EMU membership.

The 1997 budget was unveiled at the end of September and has had to fight its way through both houses of parliament in the face some 10,000 opposition amendments. The bill was finally blasted past the Senate last week thanks to a battery of confidence motions.
